c1-0-lady.prompt:
# AUDIO PROFILE
The old lady: an Englishwoman of the old school in her eighties who has run the bunker's kitchen for five years and is frightened of nothing.

## THE SCENE
Outside, in the open air. The hundred survivors walk out of the bunker's blast doors into grey daylight after five years underground, then across wet green chalk downs in Wiltshire towards a long, low, black glass building. Wind, open sky, no echo; voices close and private amid a crowd walking.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Emotion for this line: dry, flat, not looking at her; said while her hand is still on the bunting, as if it were nothing.
Style: dry, flat, deeply suspicious at first, then the softest she ever gets; in the circle, matter-of-fact and very funny without trying.
Pace: slow and deliberate, long pauses she is in no hurry to fill.
Accent: old-fashioned Received Pronunciation, as heard on the BBC in the 1950s; clipped, precise, Home Counties. Never American.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the formidable grandmother in a British drama who everyone, including the robot, does what she says.

# AUDIO PROFILE
Maddie, a small pavement delivery robot with a young woman's voice, late twenties. A real person, never robotic.

## THE SCENE
Outside, in the open air. The hundred survivors walk out of the bunker's blast doors into grey daylight after five years underground, then across wet green chalk downs in Wiltshire towards a long, low, black glass building. Wind, open sky, no echo; voices close and private amid a crowd walking.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Emotion for this line: genuinely touched, trying not to make a fuss.
Style: dry, warm and cheeky, apologetic for her boss but fond of him; quick, natural conversational rhythm, a bit of a gossip; clear articulation.
Pace: quick and chatty, with real pauses where the script marks them.
Accent: West Country, as heard in Bristol. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the cheerful local in a British comedy who turns out to be the kindest person in it.

c4-0-sandra.prompt:
# AUDIO PROFILE
Sandra, a working-class woman from Bolton, Lancashire in her fifties, married to Derek for thirty years.

## THE SCENE
Outside, in the open air. The hundred survivors walk out of the bunker's blast doors into grey daylight after five years underground, then across wet green chalk downs in Wiltshire towards a long, low, black glass building. Wind, open sky, no echo; voices close and private amid a crowd walking.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Emotion for this line: brisk, sideways, as if it is any other morning; the word is 'seat', as in the toilet seat: a long, clear 'ee'; never 'sit'.
Style: sharp, sarcastic, every line a jab; not shouting at first, then loud. Funny because she is completely serious.
Pace: quick and clipped.
Accent: Northern English, as heard in Lancashire, around Bolton. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the wife in a British sitcom row that the whole street can hear.
